articles.headline: What Sir Jim Ratcliffe really thinks of Jason Wilcox’s work at Man United
keyFacts: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martínez criticised director of football Jason Wilcox for failing to strengthen the squad during the summer transfer window.
United bosses discussed Martínez's critical comments and are assessing whether to take disciplinary action against him.
Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and other club chiefs continue to support Jason Wilcox in his role.
body: What Sir Jim Ratcliffe really thinks of Jason Wilcox’s work at Man United Manchester United suffered a 2-0 defeat at the hands of Atlético Madrid in the Champions League, delivering a performance that once again lacked intensity and cutting edge.

Lisandro Martínez could not help United keep only their second clean sheet of the season, but he channelled all that pent-up frustration into his post-match interview, taking aim at the United hierarchy.
Lisandro Martínez raises eyebrows at Manchester United
Lisandro Martínez criticised United director of football Jason Wilcox for failing to adequately strengthen the side during the summer transfer window.
The World Cup winner said he expected more from Wilcox in the summer and that the current squad is not strong enough “to be ready for this kind of night.”

Given Michael Carrick was forced to use Ayden Heaven, a central defender, at left-back and Bryan Mbuemo, a right-sided forward, as a striker against Atlético Madrid, it is hard to disagree with Martínez. Still, the move has not gone down well with some figures behind the scenes.
According to ESPN , United bosses are now assessing Martínez’s comments before deciding whether to take disciplinary action against the Argentina defender.
It is understood United bosses discussed Martínez’s comments on Wednesday.
The Argentina international is expected to find out whether he will be at the receiving end of any further action from the club on Thursday.
Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s take on Jason Wilcox’s work
Meanwhile, the report claims Wilcox retains the support of United chiefs.
It is understood that minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who was key to Wilcox’s appointment, is happy with his role within United’s hierarchy.
The former Manchester City man arrived at Old Trafford as technical director in 2024 before succeeding Dan Ashworth as director of football.

The decision to let someone of Wilcox’s limited calibre assume the responsibilities Ashworth, a hugely respected figure within the game, held seemed a risky move at the time, and the way things have unfolded to date, it is fair to say it was a terrible move.

articles.headline: “Super Unnecessary” – Kayla Harrison Slams Demetrious Johnson for Mocking UFC 332 Main Event
keyFacts: Demetrious Johnson and Israel Adesanya mocked the UFC 332 main event between Natalia Silva and Wang Cong on their podcast.
Kayla Harrison criticized Johnson for mocking the upcoming female fighters and for previously suggesting she should retire instead of fighting Amanda Nunes.
Harrison is scheduled to defend her 135-pound title against Nunes in the co-main event of UFC 334 on November 14.
body: UFC 332 was widely regarded as one of the weakest numbered cards in recent memory, at least on paper. The criticism intensified after the main event was changed at the last minute to a vacant flyweight title fight between Natalia Silva and Wang Cong .
The late change came after Valentina Shevchenko was forced to vacate her title due to shoulder and back injuries that were expected to keep her sidelined for at least a year.

Women’s MMA has also faced questions about its star power in recent years, particularly following Amanda Nunes’ departure from the sport. Naturally, the UFC 332 headliner in Salt Lake City became a talking point on Demetrious Johnson and Israel Adesanya’s Precision podcast.

Adesanya admitted that he hadn’t realized the card was being promoted as a major attraction. He also pointed out that Silva and Cong were relatively unfamiliar names without an established storyline to sell the fight. Both he and Johnson even suggested they might skip watching the UFC’s return to Salt Lake City.

When their podcast producer reminded them that Silva vs. Cong was headlining the event, the two fighters burst into laughter at the UFC’s decision. However, their reaction didn’t sit well with Kayla Harrison, one of the biggest stars in women’s MMA.
Kayla Harrison Has Strong Words for Demetrious Johnson Over UFC 332 Criticism

In a recent interview with Ariel Helwani , Harrison took particular issue with Johnson mocking the matchup between Silva and Cong. The UFC women’s bantamweight champion also brought up Johnson’s previous comments about her chances against Nunes.
She said, “I’m just kind of over (Demetrious Johnson’s) attitude. First of all, he’s the one that said I shouldn’t fight Amanda; I should retire.”

Following UFC 316 in June 2025, Harrison became the 135-pound champion after beating Julianna Pena. Johnson subsequently suggested that she should retire rather than face Nunes, believing she wouldn’t stand a chance against the former champion.

Harrison also criticized Johnson for taking shots at up-and-coming female fighters who are still trying to establish themselves in a competitive division. She argued that mocking fighters who haven’t yet become household names does little to help the sport grow.

She said, “This mindset of scarcity is detrimental to the growth of the sport. There’s enough room at the table for all of us to eat, and we don’t have to belittle, poke fun at, or put down anyone else to build our own brand. I just don’t believe in that. And especially for a retired fighter.”
Kayla Harrison shares why she took issue with Demetrious Johnson’s recent comments about Natalia Silva and Wang Cong:
“I’m just kind of over Mighty’s attitude. I’m over it.

This mindset of scarcity is detrimental to the growth of the sport. There’s enough room at the table for all of us to eat, and we don’t have to belittle or poke fun or put down anyone else in order to build our own brand.
Of course those girls are not stars yet, but do you know how you build a star? You fucking put them in the main event, and you build them.
To talk shit about them like that, I just feel is unnecessary. Super unnecessary.”
— Ariel Helwani (@arielhelwani) October 14, 2026

Harrison went on to explain why giving relatively unknown fighters opportunities in high-profile matchups can help them develop into bigger stars.

She added, “Of course, those girls are not stars yet, but you know how you build a star? You put them in the main event and build them. You have to start somewhere, so to talk s**t about them like that is just unnecessary, super unnecessary.”

Despite the criticism surrounding the lineup, UFC 332 delivered an action-packed night. The event set a record with 11 knockouts , including nine in the opening round, which also established a new record.

The main event between Cong and Silva wasn’t an instant classic, but the two flyweights put on a respectable back-and-forth contest for the vacant title. While the matchup may not have generated the excitement of a blockbuster headliner beforehand, the event itself gave fans plenty of action.

As for Harrison, she’ll soon have the chance to settle her own rivalry with Nunes. The two are scheduled to meet in the co-main event of UFC 334 on November 14, with Harrison’s 135-pound title on the line.
After Johnson questioned whether Harrison could beat Nunes, the upcoming showdown gives the champion an opportunity to prove him wrong inside the Octagon.

articles.headline: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds
keyFacts: SpaceX restricted weapon connectivity speeds on its network to 100mph on Tuesday, disrupting Ukrainian drone operations, officials said.
Elon Musk stated the US government controls Starshield speed limits, while Ukrainian officials attributed the disruption to political tensions with Washington.
The United Kingdom announced it would speed up delivery of lightweight multirole missiles to Ukraine to shoot down Russian drones.
body: - Published
Elon Musk has suggested that the US government may be behind restrictions on the speed at which some of Ukraine's weapons can travel and stay connected to SpaceX's Starlink internet network.

Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to guide drones to Russian targets and also protect its own skies, but on Tuesday night Ukraine said unexpected new speed limits were disrupting its battlefield missions.
An adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky said he believed the restrictions were not a coincidence and were related to the latest strains between Kyiv and Washington.

Musk said that Starshield, the military-grade sister service to Starlink, is controlled by the US government, and "any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately [the US president]".

Musk - writing on X - had been responding to pleas from Ukrainian officials to restore connectivity, including from Zelensky who told UK media: "I hope that it's a mistake, maybe [a] huge technical problem. I don't know, but we are asking to... switch [it] on."
Starlink, which is owned by Musk's SpaceX, restricted speed limits on Tuesday night to 100mph (160km/h), meaning any weapons that travelled faster than that lost connectivity to the network.
It had been partially restored by Wednesday evening, Ukraine's former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov said.
"Removing Starshield's speed limit entirely is now critical for Ukraine's defense," he wrote on X, thanking Elon Musk and asking for his "continued support".
About an hour later, Musk replied to that post, defending his company's involvement.
"Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," he wrote.
Musk added that Starlink is for "civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company".
The US government has not commented.
In the early hours of Thursday, Russian strikes killed two people in the Dnipropetrovsk region, regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha said.

While both companies are owned by Musk's SpaceX, Starlink is a civilian service that uses satellites in low Earth orbit to provide internet access, particularly in remote areas, while Starshield is designed for government and military use.

The restrictions on Tuesday night came as Russia launched deadly attacks against Ukraine that killed several people in Kyiv, officials said, and hit communications and energy facilities used by Ukraine's military.
Zelensky said it was "one of the largest attacks" from Russia, and while "a significant part of the drones were shot down" there were "also hits".
At least 600,000 people across Ukraine were left without electricity, and residents said they received no warning of incoming drones before they hit.
"It is clear that this action cannot be a coincidence and is related to the current political situation," Zelensky's adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov wrote on Telegram on Wednesday morning.
US President Donald Trump has grown increasingly frustrated towards Ukraine as it continues to strike Russian energy facilities.
Zelensky has said that the US threatened to restrict intelligence sharing if he did not sign up to Trump's energy ceasefire, but on Tuesday, Trump denied this.

Late on Wednesday, Musk wrote on X, responding to a post saying that Zelensky would not end the war until Russia was defeated, "And so the slaughter continues â¦ Time for Zelensky to go". He has made similar comments before.
Earlier this week he said said: "I agree, time for Ukraine to get a new leader," after Trump said it was "time for Ukraine to get a new president".
Since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022 the country has been under martial law, meaning elections have been suspended.
Speaking during a visit to London on Wednesday, Zelensky agreed that he had felt betrayed after the US made a deal with Russia to import 300,000 tonnes of its diesel.
"Really yes... but it's a little bit more complicated than just my emotions or my feelings," Zelensky said, when asked by UK journalist Piers Morgan if he felt betrayed.
During his one-day visit, Zelensky was greeted with a hug by UK PM Andy Burnham at Downing Street and held an audience with King Charles.
Ahead of the president's arrival, No 10 announced it would speed up delivery of lightweight multirole missiles to Ukraine, which have been used to bring down Russian drones.
"We are behind you and that will not change," Burnham told Zelensky.

articles.headline: Figma announces new features to define how agents work on its platform
keyFacts: Design platform Figma announced new features, including a Markdown-based editor called Figma Specs, to help AI agents adhere to brand design rules.
Figma made its code layers feature available in public beta, allowing users to ask agents to turn designs into code or iterate on prototypes.
Figma chief design officer Loredana Crisan stated that the platform aims to help software teams decide what to build and ship using AI.
body: Design platform Figma announced a new Markdown-based editor to help define a company’s design, bring in design and code libraries, and integrate with the Payload headless content management system during the company’s first Config event in India. Through some of these features, the company aims to provide a definition for its own and third-party agents to adhere to a brand’s design rules better while creating with AI.

The company debuted a new feature called Figma Specs, which is a markdown editor that lets users define their design language in a simple way. The document can serve as a reference for teams and agents while designing in Figma. Specs can exist as a standalone file in Figma or can co-exist within the canvas. Apart from acting as a text editor, users can reference other Figma elements, such as elements on the canvas and embed FigJam diagrams, code layers, and designs.

What’s more, teams can bring in more context about design, including design libraries, code libraries, and guidelines to manage context for the design system. Agents can also refer to this centralized system to adhere to rules.

In the past week, the company made its agent on canvas available to a wider user base. However, given the non-deterministic nature of AI, the company is providing tools to steer it towards more predictable outcomes.

Figma also made its code layers feature, which adds coding to designs on canvas for more interactive prototypes. The company announced this feature in private beta back in June. At its India event this week, the company is making the function available in public beta to let more users test it out. Users can also ask the agent to turn a design into code or change a part of the code to iterate on a prototype.

“We see Figma as the place where software teams come to decide what they build and ship. And so for that, I think one of the key things to keep in mind about what AI has changed and what it made available is the ability to build,” Figma’s chief design officer Loredana Crisan told TechCrunch. “There are 17-times more lines of code being produced today than in the past. But when you’re looking at releases, only 1.3-times more releases. A lot of that code actually is not necessarily built to ship, but really built to discover what the product is. It’s built to design.”
The company said it is also supporting over 20 new tools with its MCP, including Open Code, Dia, Grok Bot, and Indian AI startup Sarvam.

Last year, Figma acquired open-source headless CMS Payload. Now, the company is integrating it with its Figma Make product for generating dynamic websites and directly managing content. The company said that Payload’s downloads have increased sixfold in the last 12 months.

The company opened its first office in India late last year with sales, partnership, go-to-market, and product support functions. Figma said that the country is its biggest market in terms of users outside the United States. The company noted that the platform works with 40% of India’s top 100 companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange.

articles.headline: Anthropic flags revenue surge to investors ahead of stock market debut
keyFacts: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic reported a 45% revenue surge to $16.8bn in the third quarter according to BBC understands.
The figures were revealed to prospective investors during a briefing ahead of an expected stock market listing before the end of the year.
Shares in several major technology companies fell globally following concerns over heavy spending on AI infrastructure and industry expectations.
body: - Published
Artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic saw its revenue surge by 45% to $16.8bn (Â£12.7bn) in the three months to the end of September, the BBC understands.

The figures were revealed by the Claude-developer as it briefed prospective investors on Wednesday at its headquarters in San Francisco as it lays the groundwork for a stock market listing, which is expected to take place before the end of the year.

It comes as some tech stocks, including firms that make the chips and other hardware that power data centres, have fallen in recent days over concerns about the hundreds of billions of dollars being spent on AI infrastructure.
An Anthropic spokesperson declined to comment.
Anthropic's revenue has risen in successive quarters this year, from $4.7bn in the first three months to $11.6bn the following period.
The company also reportedly said that it made a profit for the second quarter in a row.
Its revenue figures, along with those of rival OpenAI, offer an important gauge of the AI industry's growth and ability to finance the infrastructure needed to develop the technology.
Stocks in some US technology companies fell on Wednesday over concerns around investments in AI.
Share in chip makers - including AMD, Nvidia and Intel - fell sharply.

In Asia, shares in Japanese tech investment firm Softbank fell by more than 9% on Thursday morning. South Korean semiconductor giants were also down, with Samsung falling by 9.4% and SK Hynix dropping 10.8%.
Tech-heavy indexes in the region were also down. Trading on South Korea's Kospi and Kosdaq was temporarily halted after falling by more than 8%, while Japan's Nikkei 225 fell by over 5%.
The falls come after remarks by Hock Tan, the chief executive of US tech manufacturer Broadcom, over AI spending.
Tan said at an conference in Singapore on Monday that many investors have "no clue" and have set "extreme expectations only to find out that it's almost like they are in a casino".
There also been concerns over the safety of AI models.
OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said in September that his company will not go public this year as it addresses concerns about the technology's safety.
The ChatGPT-developer is also eyeing a bumper stock market listing, which is expected to value the firm at more than $1tn.
Anthropic has also been vocal about AI's risks, with its chief executive Dario Amodei calling on the pace of development to slow down.
The company has continued expanding globally, opening an office in Singapore on Wednesday.

articles.headline: India urges Russia, Ukraine to protect Black Sea shipping
keyFacts: India urged Russia and Ukraine to protect Black Sea commercial shipping following recent attacks on merchant vessels.
The conflict endangers Indian crews and supply chains, as India represents over twelve percent of the global seafaring workforce.
New Delhi said discussions are underway, though Russia has not publicly endorsed India's proposed safe-passage arrangement.
body: India has urged both Russia and Ukraine to ensure safe passage for commercial shipping through the Black Sea as attacks on merchant vessels put Indian seafarers at risk and threaten to disrupt vital food and energy supplies.
New Delhi says discussions with both sides are under way.

"The targeting of commercial shipping and seafarers in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways must be restored at the earliest," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said last week.

India accounts for more than 12% of the global seafaring workforce, with 311,936 maritime professionals, according to a 2026 industry report. And attacks on commercial vessels in and around the Black Sea in recent months have highlighted the risks facing civilian crews.

The Turkish-owned MV Royad Mammadov, a cargo ship carrying grain from Ukraine, caught fire and sank following an attack on Monday, killing two crew members. The three Indian nationals aboard the vessel survived, but sustained injuries and were taken to Romania to receive medical treatment.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia for launching the strike.
The Defense Ministry in Moscow separately said it had struck two Ukrainian cargo vessels in the Black Sea but did not specifically identify the ships.

The Liberian-flagged oil tanker Aframax Rio was also recently attacked by unmanned vessels off Russia's Black Sea coast near Sochi, according to Russian authorities. The vessel was carrying 23 Indians, but all of them were rescued.
Can diplomacy deliver safety?

Anil Wadhwa, a former Indian diplomat, said India's proposal to halt attacks on commercial shipping in the Black Sea covered energy infrastructure, safe passage for grain and energy exports, and an end to strikes on merchant vessels.
"Securing an ironclad guarantee depends entirely on a broader cessation of hostilities between Russia and Ukraine in the maritime theater," Wadhwa told DW.
India's close relations with Russia and expanding engagement with Ukraine give New Delhi access to both sides, but do not guarantee either will honor a shipping arrangement.
Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has described India's proposal for a possible ceasefire with Russia as the "broadest" of the four offers Kyiv has received.
Russia has not publicly endorsed a binding safe-passage deal proposed by India, despite welcoming New Delhi's peace efforts.

Rajan Kumar of the Center for Russian and Central Asian Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University said India could use its diplomatic leverage with Moscow to help bring the two sides towards an agreement.
"India could play a constructive role in facilitating dialogue between Russia and Ukraine, particularly on the issue of ensuring the safety of commercial shipping in the Black Sea," Kumar told DW.
Working with other powers to reach a deal
He argued that India should also work with other influential countries from the Global South, particularly China, Brazil and South Africa.

"A coordinated approach with these countries could enhance their collective diplomatic leverage and strengthen their capacity to persuade both parties to adopt mutually acceptable arrangements for maritime security," said Kumar.
India's initiative comes as US President Donald Trump announced an "energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine over the weekend, although its scope and implementation mechanism remain unclear.

Harsh Pant, vice president of the New Delhi-based think tank Observer Research Foundation, said Trump's intervention could help India's efforts but might produce a narrower agreement that fails to address New Delhi's wider concerns.

"The energy ceasefire could be an initial confidence-building measure, whereas a Black Sea shipping arrangement requires additional commitments on attacks against merchant vessels, ports, maritime routes and the security of commercial traffic," Pant told DW.
"India need not compete with Washington for the public credit of mediation. It could instead press for the inclusion of broader maritime provisions in any US agreement.”
Will India face a higher import bill?
Wadhwa said the proposed energy truce could also benefit Indian seafarers if it secured safe passage for energy cargoes.

"Although Ukraine alleges that the Russians have already breached this so-called truce, there will be pressure on both sides to allow energy cargoes safe passage. India is bound to gain as far as its crews are concerned in such a scenario," he said.
The disruption to Black Sea shipping also has other implications for India such as delays in shipments of key commodities and higher transport costs.

"A prolonged Black Sea disruption would elevate India's import bill mainly via higher freight on Russian crude and constrained soft oil supplies, with the strongest near-term transmission to domestic edible oil prices and food inflation," said Lekha Chakraborty, professor at the National Institute of Public Finance and Policy.

articles.headline: How to defeat Medusa in Castlevania Belmont's Curse
keyFacts: Medusa is an early boss in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse located in the Holy Innocents' Cemetery region.
Players must defeat Medusa to obtain keys for the catacombs gate, the Prophetess's Key, and the Petrifying Gaze arcana.
The guide states that defeating Medusa requires memorizing her attack rotation, using platforms, and hiding behind large rocks during her ultimate move.
body: Medusa, also known as the Prophetess, is one of the first three bosses in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse that you face. You must defeat her to obtain the keys to open the gate to the catacombs. The game won't tell you where you can find these enemies, forcing you to explore every room in the initial maps for hints that will lead you to the boss rooms.
Below, we explain how to beat Medusa in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse and where to find her.
[Ed. note: This guide uses screenshots captured from a build still in development at the time of writing.]
Where to find the Prophetess in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse

You can find the Prophetess in the Holy Innocents' Cemetery region, left of Paris Streets. Early in the game, the best way to reach the cemetery is to head left from the Street of the Tomb Masons area in Paris Streets.

In the Holy Innocents' Cemetery region, keep going left until you reach the Fountain of the Lost. Drop in the water to descend into the Serpent's Lair area below. The Prophetess's boss arena is the last room on the left, past the Mirror of Life on the right side.
How to beat Medusa in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse

The secret to defeating Medusa in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse is to memorize her attack rotation and become familiar with swapping between the platforms in the arena. Defeating her not only grants you the Prophetess' Key, but also the Petrifying Gaze arcana. Her moveset consists of three basic attacks:

- Slam attack: Medusa attacks you by slamming her arm onto the platform in front of her, then follows up with a slash attack. She always raises one of her arms for a few seconds before unleashing this attack. You have enough time to hit her a couple of times while she charges the attack, but eventually you will need to jump off of the platform. Practice dropping off the platform to avoid the attack, then coming back using the whip on the purple anchor to get back up.

- Petrifying attack: Medusa can release a petrifying beam, which you can identify as she charges the attack and small glowing particles fly toward her. To avoid the attack, turn Rose's back to Medusa.
- Tail attack: Throughout the fight, Medusa will use her tail to attack you if you stay on the lower platforms.

First, try to memorize these three attacks and how to deal with them. Once you can dodge them without any trouble, your goal is to stay on the upper platform closest to Medusa and look for the openings to attack her.

After you have attacked Medusa enough to deplete about 25% of her life bar, she will perform her ultimate move. The screen will shake, her tail will slam both lower platforms a few times, and Medusa will unleash a sequence of slash attacks in front of her. As soon as the screen starts shaking, move to the upper platform on the opposite side of Medusa. Wait for her tail to return to the water, then look for a large rock that has fallen from the ceiling of the arena. It will always be on the lower platform opposite Medusa. Quickly hide behind it. Otherwise, you won't avoid the multiple beams coming out of her hair, and you will die.

Medusa repeats her ultimate move a few times during the fight. Although she keeps the same pattern, after the second time, small rocks will start to fall from the ceiling that can damage you. Try to avoid them but prioritize hiding behind the large rock.

articles.headline: Argentina’s Milei backs Trump for US midterms, calls vote crucial for West
keyFacts: Argentine President Javier Milei backed US President Donald Trump ahead of US midterm elections, calling the vote crucial for the West.
Analysts argued that previous support from Trump and a 20-billion-dollar currency swap helped Milei succeed in Argentine legislative elections.
Milei is scheduled to address the US Chamber of Commerce on Thursday during his visit to Washington.
body: Argentine President Javier Milei has urged his ally, US President Donald Trump, to come out of the United States midterm elections in a stronger position, calling the vote important for the West as a whole.
Milei made the appeal on Wednesday at a Hispanic Heritage gala in Washington, where a Hispanic association gave him an award, ahead of November’s vote.
Conservatives, he said, “cannot give an inch in our reconquest of the hemisphere”, according to Agence France-Presse (AFP).
Milei flew into the US capital on Wednesday for meetings with investors and the gala. He is due to address the US Chamber of Commerce on Thursday.
Milei’s lifeline
Trump firmly backed Milei a year ago, when his government also faced crucial legislative elections. He has called Milei his “favorite president”.
That backing, together with a currency swap agreement with the US Treasury, helped Milei to success in those polls, analysts have argued.

The centrepiece of the package, announced by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, was a $20bn swap with Argentina’s central bank, in which the US exchanged dollars for pesos. The swap came shortly after Milei’s party lost a key provincial election.

Trump made clear at the time that the support hinged on a Milei victory. “I’m with this man because his philosophy is correct,” he said ahead of a White House lunch with the Argentine leader. “If he wins, we’re staying with him. And if he doesn’t win, we’re gone.”

Trump also warned that the US would not be “generous” if Milei lost. The remarks unsettled Argentine markets, with the main stock index giving up earlier gains and falling about 2 percent, The Associated Press reported.
The package drew criticism in the US. Democratic lawmakers accused Trump of prioritising a foreign bailout while the US government was shut down.

articles.headline: Brewers go one win from World Series as back-to-back homers sink Dodgers
keyFacts: The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-2 on Wednesday night to take a 3-0 lead in the National League Championship Series.
Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back home runs off Blake Snell in the seventh inning to reclaim the lead for Milwaukee.
Game 4 of the series takes place on Thursday at Dodger Stadium.
body: Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back home runs off Blake Snell to reclaim the lead in the seventh inning as the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-2 on Wednesday night to take a commanding 3-0 lead in the National League Championship Series.

The Dodgers had just taken a 2-1 lead in the bottom of the sixth before being stunned. The loss pushed the two-time defending World Series champions to the brink of elimination. They had trailed 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series only once previously in franchise history, when they were swept by the Baltimore Orioles in the 1966 World Series.
Game 4 is Thursday at Dodger Stadium.

Snell had retired 14 consecutive batters entering the seventh. The two-time Cy Young Award winner’s first pitch of the game was driven out of the park by Jackson Chourio, and his last was Mitchell’s solo shot.

Andrew Vaughn drew a seven-pitch walk to open the seventh and was replaced by pinch-runner Christian Yelich. Bauers followed with a 412ft drive to right field on the 11th pitch of the at-bat, giving Milwaukee a 3-2 lead as much of the Brewers’ dugout spilled on to the field in celebration. Mitchell came up next and launched a 428ft shot to right-center, chasing Snell.
Snell allowed four runs on four hits over six-plus innings, striking out nine and walking two.

The Brewers are on the verge of sweeping the Dodgers in a reversal of last year’s NLCS, when Los Angeles eliminated Milwaukee in four games. The Brewers have never beaten the Dodgers in three previous postseason series.

Milwaukee extended their lead to 5-2 in the eighth on a wild pitch by Justin Wrobleski that scored Brice Turang, who had reached on an infield single to third and advanced on William Contreras’ single. They added another run on Joey Ortiz’s two-strike RBI single in the ninth.
The offensively starved Dodgers had taken their first lead of the night, 2-1, on Will Smith’s two-run double off reliever Abner Uribe in the sixth.

Uribe, who replaced rookie starter Robert Gasser, loaded the bases with walks to Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker and Shohei Ohtani. Smith, who entered the game batting .043, doubled to left-center for his first hit of the NLCS.
DL Hall replaced Uribe, allowing one hit and striking out two before handing the ball to Trevor Megill in the eighth.
The Dodgers had fallen behind almost immediately when Chourio homered off Snell’s first pitch, with fans still making their way to their seats.
Mitchell then walked and Cooper Pratt singled in the second before Snell retired 14 consecutive batters, six by strikeout, only to unravel in the seventh.
Los Angeles put runners on base in all but three innings but struggled to bring them home. They have yet to hit a home run in the NLCS.
Ohtani went 1 for 2 with a walk while batting sixth, his lowest spot in the lineup since joining the Dodgers three years ago.

articles.headline: Trump announces advanced weapons testing ‘super range’ in Montana
keyFacts: President Donald Trump announced the military will establish a new testing range in Montana for advanced weapons and technologies.
Trump made the announcement during a rally to boost Montana Republican candidates Aaron Flint and Kurt Alme.
Trump also stated Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will invest three billion dollars to help ten thousand Montana homebuyers.
body: President Donald Trump on Wednesday announced the Department of War is establishing a new military testing range in Montana as he sought to boost Republican candidates in the state at a campaign rally.

The president said the Pentagon would establish a “new super range for testing advanced weapons and technologies,” including possible autonomous weapons, space and electronic warfare technology, supersonics, and hypersonics, during the event at Majestic Valley Arena in Kalispell. Trump’s latest announcement comes after he similarly revealed plans for a new submarine repair center in Ohio during a recent rally in the battleground state.
“Montana will help ensure the American military always reigns supreme,” Trump told attendees at the Montana rally, in remarks where he promised the Iran war would “end very quickly.”

The Kalispell rally sought to boost GOP congressional candidate Aaron Flint, who is in a tight race for a toss-up House seat against Democrat Sam Forstag. Republican Senate candidate Kurt Alme, who holds a firm polling lead in his race against Democratic candidate Alani Bankhead and independent candidate Seth Bodnar to succeed Sen. Steve Daines (R-MT), also attended the event.
During the rally, Trump made another announcement, revealing that Fannie Mae, a government-sponsored mortgage financier, would invest billions in Montana to help residents buy their own homes.

“Under my leadership, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will be investing $3 billion in Montana mortgages to help 10,000 Montana homebuyers achieve their American dream,” the president said before recognizing Chairman of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac Bill Pulte, who was at the rally.

Trump sought to emphasize what he characterized as the strengths of his administration during the speech. He said Washington had ushered in significant economic gains since he took office in January 2025, arguing the United States has “the lowest level of poverty individually, … the highest level of individual wealth, and more people are working in our country today than ever before.” Trump told voters they have a “very simple” choice in the November elections before attacking “Democrat communists” who he warned would raise the cost of living.
President Donald Trump greets U.S. House candidate Aaron Flint at a campaign rally at Majestic Valley Arena, Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026, in Kalispell, Montana. (AP Photo/Alex Brandon)
TRUMP SAYS GOVERNMENT LEAKERS ‘SHOULD BE SHOT’

“You can vote for the radical left Democrat communist to loot your wealth, raise your taxes by $5 trillion,” Trump said. “It’s a crazy age, but they want to annihilate your voters, decimate Montana jobs, take away your guns, mutilate your children, give 25 million illegal aliens amnesty, and then give them the right to vote.”

“All my life, I’ve watched politicians — I’ve always found it fascinating. Little did I know I was going to be doing this, but all my life I’ve watched them say, Democrat and Republican, ‘We will lower your taxes. We will never raise your taxes. We will cut your taxes in half,’” he continued. “That’s everybody. This group is saying we will raise your taxes, and you’re supposed to vote for them. This is a crazy age, isn’t it?”

articles.headline: Texas Democrat James Talarico faces grilling from voters at town hall in tight Senate race
keyFacts: Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico answered undecided voters' questions on faith and abortion during a CNN town hall.
Talarico and Republican nominee Ken Paxton are in a close race, with recent polls showing Talarico with a narrow lead.
Democrats have not won a Texas Senate seat since the late 1980s, but they hope Talarico will persuade independents and Republicans.
body: James Talarico, the Texas Democratic nominee for Senate, sat face to face with several undecided voters who grilled him on a slew of contentious issues including Israel’s military campaign in Gaza, abortion and foreign aid, during a CNN town hall on Wednesday evening.
One voter, a devout small business owner, questioned the authenticity of Talarico’s faith, referencing a past remark where he described God as nonbinary.

“When I said that, I was being provocative and I want to admit that and come clean about that,” Talarico responded. “What I was saying is actually not controversial theologically: the idea that we can’t define God using human categories. Not only did I say that, but the late Charlie Kirk said that – the late Pope Benedict said that.”
Talarico added that he was receptive to feedback from Christians.

Jodi Hunt, a self-described single-issue voter, probed Talarico’s pro-choice stance, asking: “How would you convince me as a Catholic voter that I can trust you would protect the most innocent among us?”
Talarico described the Bible as being silent on abortion, to which Hunt countered quoting “Thou shalt not kill”.

“We may have different, moral conclusions when it comes to this particular ethical question, but we actually have the same public policy goal,” Talarico said, framing abortion as a public health issue that could be solved with a reduction in unplanned pregnancies.
During the night, Talarico cast himself as a moderate, who would put the needs of Texans over party allegiances. He railed against the ultra-wealthy, framing them as the common enemy.

Talarico and the Republican nominee, Ken Paxton, are locked in a competitive race to become Texas’s next US senator, with most recent polls showing Talarico with a narrow lead over Paxton. (Paxton declined an invitation to appear on CNN, host Erin Burnett said at the start of the town hall.)

Though Democrats have not won a Senate seat in the state since the late 1980s, they’re hoping Talarico’s newcomer energy and popular appeal will persuade independents and Republicans fed up with Donald Trump’s second term – or turned off by Paxton’s many scandals.

Over the weekend, Talarico became the subject of a disinformation campaign after he was absent from the campaign trail for more than a week. While Talarico’s campaign repeatedly said the candidate was sick with a bad case of the flu, conservative influencers falsely accused him of receiving medical treatment at a mental health facility in Ohio.
The rumor was further propelled by Paxton and Trump, who sought to fuel skepticism about Talarico’s health and fitness for office.
The Democratic candidate denied the false allegations after returning to the campaign trail last week, noting he had never been to Ohio.

“False claims got millions of views online and this is an example of what I call the ‘rage economy’,” Talarico said during the town hall. “Billionaires who own these platforms get rich. We all get angry and nobody’s life gets any better. Conspiracy theories don’t put food on the table, put gas in the tank, or improve our communities.”

Paxton, meanwhile, has been battling his own controversies. A series of leaked audio recordings – made during a closed-door meeting – have been posted online and revealed him being critical of his own party and campaign leaders in DC.

Paxton entered the race with a history of scandals. He was impeached by the Texas state legislature in 2023 on allegations including bribery and abuse of public trust, though he was later acquitted. Paxton’s wife of almost four decades, Angela Paxton, then filed for divorce in 2025 on “biblical grounds”, citing adultery.
But Trump endorsed Paxton to run against Talarico, passing up incumbent Republican John Cornyn.

articles.headline: Talarico debates voters in table-for-two setting at televised town hall
keyFacts: Texas Senate Democratic nominee James Talarico debated six voters one-on-one during a televised CNN town hall on Wednesday.
Talarico addressed voter questions regarding abortion, the national debt, his personal faith, and his opposition to transgender surgeries for minors.
Talarico and his Republican opponent Ken Paxton are locked in a tight Senate race as early voting nears.
body: Texas Senate Democratic nominee James Talarico sat face-to-face with voters as he was grilled on a wide range of topics, including abortion , antisemitism , the SAVE America Act , the national debt, transgender surgeries for minors, and his faith during a CNN town hall on Wednesday evening.
Talarico engaged in a debate with six voters from across the political spectrum, with each coming to the stage to sit down across the table from the candidate.
The conversations remained cordial, despite vehement disagreements at times, with Talarico and the voters engaging in polite small talk before delving into, at times, heavy topics.

The discussion began with a question about abortion from a Catholic professor, who suggested she was a single-issue voter on the issue of life. Talarico outlined ways both parties could come together to find solutions.

“If we can join together to make sure that we have scientifically valid sex education, age-appropriate sex education, if we can make sure that folks who need contraception can get it, if we can make sure that everyone has healthcare, something the Catholic Church has led on, then we know that that reduces the number of abortions because you can look at the research and you see that certain policy levers like sex education, like healthcare can actually reduce the number of abortions,” he responded.

The attendees also peppered Talarico with questions about voter ID and the national debt. Talarico said he supports voter ID as long as it is “fair.” When asked about the rising national debt, he pointed to “closing billionaire loopholes” and criticized Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act and the war in Iran as contributors to the growing debt.

“This big ugly bill that was passed a year ago gave $3 trillion in tax cuts to the top 1% people who don’t need it,” Talarico said. “Nothing against the top 1%, but they don’t need any help, and that money could go toward closing the deficit and tackling the debt. And then I’ll mention one more: We can close the deficit and tackle the debt by ending this disastrous war in Iran that is costing us $1 billion a day.”

Talarico also addressed previous comments he has walked back when a Republican voter pressed him on his faith. When a woman asked whether he believed the Bible was the authoritative word of God, he immediately responded, “Yes.”

He told the woman, who expressed concerns over Talarico previously calling God “nonbinary,” that it’s “OK if you and I have disagreements about our interpretations of Scripture — or certainly about political and policy topics. That should be encouraged, not discouraged. And we can do that as we’re called to do in Scripture.”

On his previous comment about God being nonbinary, Talarico said he “was being provocative and I want to admit that and come clean about that. But I think what I was saying is actually not controversial theologically, the idea that we can’t define God using human categories. Not only did I say that, but the late Charlie Kirk said that, the late Pope Benedict said that.”
“And so, yes, I was doing it maybe in an annoying way. I can admit that,” Talarico conceded.

He also engaged with a voter who believed government should not be involved in someone’s decision to receive “gender-affirming surgeries,” even if that person is a minor. Talarico said in a recent interview with Fox News that he did not support transgender surgeries for minors, and he reaffirmed that position Wednesday night.
Talarico concluded the debate portion of the town hall by taking a firm stance against antisemitism while maintaining his criticism of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

“I have stood by Jewish leaders in central Texas against antisemitism,” he said. “I’ve stood against hate in all its forms, because I believe that all of us should feel welcome here in Texas, no matter our religious beliefs.”
“As a former teacher, seeing the death and the destruction in Gaza, seeing what’s happening to children in particular, makes me sick to my stomach,” he added.
TALARICO SAYS HE WOULDN’T CHANGE HOW HE HANDLED NINE-DAY FLU ABSENCE

His Republican opponent, Attorney General Ken Paxton, was largely an afterthought during the 90-minute forum, with voters instead probing Talarico on his own policy positions. At the end of the town hall, Talarico mentioned Paxton by name, calling him the “most corrupt politician in Texas.” The two remained locked in a tight race as early voting nears with Talarico having a slight edge in most polls.

“Ken Paxton has increased his net worth by $27 million,” Talarico concluded. “He now owns 15 homes, while most Texans can’t afford one, he has taken bribes from wealthy special interests, including half a million dollars from data center companies. All while he sells us out when he makes public policy, we cannot afford Ken Paxton’s corruption.”

articles.headline: James Talarico ruthlessly fact-checked by voter after claiming Bible is ‘silent’ on abortion at CNN town hall
keyFacts: Catholic voter Jody Hunt challenged Democratic Senate hopeful James Talarico after he stated the Bible is silent on abortion during a town hall.
Talarico claimed Texas's abortion ban harms women, while Hunt argued that abortion violates the biblical commandment against killing.
Talarico holds a narrow polling lead over Republican Ken Paxton in Texas, where Democrats have not won a Senate seat since 1988.
body: Democratic Senate hopeful James Talarico was ruthlessly fact-checked by a Catholic voter during a Texas town hall Wednesday after he claimed the Bible doesn’t take a stance on abortion.

Talarico, a Christian seminarian and state lawmaker, attempted to convince the self-described “one-issue voter,” Jody Hunt, that his pro-choice position is compatible with her faith because “the Bible is silent on the issue of abortion.”
Hunt, respectfully, wasn’t buying it.
She allowed Talarico to finish his point that “certain policy levers” — absent banning the procedure — can reduce abortions nationwide, before her mic-drop moment.
“I just want to add that the Bible is not silent on abortion. There is the 10 Commandments: ‘Thou shall not kill,’” Hunt shot back.
She added, “And as Catholics, we take great insult, I guess sometimes, when it’s described that way.”
Hunt further noted that Talarico’s call for expanding access to contraception and what he described as “age-appropriate sex education” is a “very trying thing” for Catholics.

“We believe the parents are the primary educators of our children, and so, one of the things that we really struggle with is having any government interference with how we educate our children,” she said. “So I know we’re going to agree to disagree on that, but I do appreciate your comments on tending to the life from the womb to the tomb, and I think that’s one common ground we can come to.”
Talarico continued to defend his stance, explaining that he doesn’t view the termination of a pregnancy as a violation of the Bible’s fundamental principles.

“If I believed that abortion was murder, that it violated the 10 Commandments, then I wouldn’t support it,” he said, claiming that the current abortion ban in Texas has resulted in “women dying in emergency room parking lots.”
“And so, if we are authentically pro-life, I think we should be disturbed by the outcomes of this extreme abortion ban,” Talarico argued.
The back-and-forth took place during a period in the town hall, hosted by CNN and Jubilee, when voters were allowed to come up to the stage and sit directly across from the candidate to debate him.
Talarico faced several questions from voters about his faith, voter ID laws, the national debt, and transgender procedures for minors during the hour-and-a-half-long forum.
The moderator, CNN’s Erin Burnett, noted that Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton declined an invitation to participate in the town hall.

Lawler, however, pointed out the man has a lengthy criminal rap sheet and was seen by some as a danger to his community. He also argued the shooting would never have happened had local law enforcement not been barred from handing him over to ICE by New York's sanctuary laws .
He said Conley "supports making New York a sanctuary state, prohibits cooperation between local law enforcement and federal immigration officials."

Lawler later pivoted the discussion to Sheridan Gorman, the college student from his district who was killed while out with her friends near her campus in Chicago earlier this year. The illegal immigrant accused of killing her was previously charged with shoplifting, but Chicago sanctuary laws prevent local law enforcement from handing him over to ICE.
Conley called Gorman's death "an atrocious crime" while repeatedly pointing out it took place in Chicago.
Lawler attempted to intervene multiple times to call it "preventable," to which an irate Conley responded, "Can I finish?"
"And I do support federal agents and federal law enforcement, federal immigration enforcement, making sure that we deport violent citizens," she said.
DHS BOSS REVEALS OVAL OFFICE PLAN TO 'WITHHOLD FUNDING' FROM SANCTUARY CITIES AFTER AGGRESSIVE NEW YORK BUST
Lawler then argued, however, that Conley's support of sanctuary policies runs counter to that.

"If you think he should have been deported when he was arrested for shoplifting, he should have been turned over to ICE. Under the new law that you support, he will not be turned over to ICE, and he will be released under cashless bail," Lawler said.
It prompted the moderator to step in, telling Lawler there was no "cross-examination round."
Elsewhere in the debate, Lawler accused Conley of having "literally just lied" that Lawler voted with Trump "100% of the time."

"I've been rated the third most independent member of my conference. And I have taken on the president on numerous issues, including lifting the cap on SALT, including extending Haitian TPS , including passing an extension for the ACA enhanced premium tax credit despite his objections," Lawler said.
Earlier in the debate, Conley tried to accuse Lawler of supporting tax breaks for companies that build data centers as part of the One Big Beautiful Bill.

Lawler shot back, "I know you just moved here from Virginia, so it's hard for you to understand the local communities, but the fact is ... the provision you referenced in the Working Families Tax Cut Act is $80 billion for 100% expensing for every business in America to expense plant, property and equipment.

"Are you against our small businesses in the Hudson Valley being able to expense their plant, property and equipment and hire more people? Your attack on that rings hollow. You clearly don't understand what's actually in the tax bill. And part of the problem is you don't pay property taxes."
A mid the drama were moments of civility.
Both candidates shook hands after their spirited debate and thanked each other for appearing. Lawler also thanked Conley for her military service.
The district is a pivotal one for control of the House next year. Lawler is one of three House Republicans who won a district that former Vice President Kamala Harris also won in 2024.
And in an election that's expected to be brutal for the GOP, both sides are pouring millions of dollars into the fight.

articles.headline: Nancy Mace: AI Makes Public Execution A-OK
keyFacts: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced plans to livestream Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan's December execution by firing squad.
Representative Nancy Mace dismissed terrorist propaganda concerns regarding the broadcast, claiming extremist groups already use artificial intelligence.
The president stated that showing the execution might deter other people from committing similar acts.
body: Nancy Mace (R-S.C.) had a mystifying take on the Pentagon’s plans for a public execution during a Wednesday appearance on CNN.

Asked if there was a risk that livestreaming Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan’s death by firing squad could be used as propaganda for terrorist groups, she said, “Well, they’re using AI these days. They don’t need a real-world example when they’re using AI in all of their propaganda.”

Mace’s very literal logic didn’t address wider concerns government officials have reportedly been considering about how broadcasting Hasan’s execution could fuel anti-American sentiment, especially among Islamic extremist groups.

After killing 13 service members and injuring over 30 in the 2009 shooting, Hasan reportedly told mental health professionals he intended to die in the attacks for the jihadist cause and “would still be a martyr” if convicted and executed.

Mace followed her AI propaganda argument with an even weaker point, adding, “I have a hard time buying, too, from people on the left who celebrated the assassination of Charlie Kirk, for example, who spread that video far and wide all over the internet of this horrific murder, now condemning an execution in this manner. It’s just very hypocritical, too.”
While footage of Kirk’s September 2025 murder was widely circulated online, posts came from supporters, critics and general gawkers alike.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth first announced his intention to livestream Hasan’s December execution last week, triggering questions about the optics and ethics from both inside and outside the administration.
“There are two thoughts: don’t show it, and show it,” the president told reporters on Saturday. “Because you know, by showing it, maybe other people won’t be doing what he did.”

body: If you’re headed to Austin, Texas, for next week’s Formula 1 United States Grand Prix, you won’t want to miss the city’s other highlights – if nothing else, you’ll need to find good barbecue. Apple is adding another dimension to the Texas capital by applying its Detailed City Experience treatment in Apple Maps, including the Circuit of the Americas track where the race is held each year.

Apple enhanced Maps’ Austin layout with detailed 3D day and night renderings of landmarks such as The Paramount Theater, Sixth Street, the Texas State Capitol building and Terry Black’s BBQ. Navigation improvements include streets with lanes (including bus and bike lanes) marked and more accurate elevation.

The race venue marks the track’s turns, shows 3D versions of the grandstands and pit building, as well as the admission entry points. It also includes flourishes such as the stars-and-stripes design of the runoff areas. (But not the World’s Largest Cowboy Hat, alas, which is still being constructed for the event.)
More from CNET

Apple, which is the official US broadcaster for F1 races on Apple TV, previously applied the Detailed City Experience glow-up to Monaco, which hosts one of the most storied F1 races of the entire tournament (several top racers call Monaco home), as well as the Albert Park Grand Prix Circuit in Melbourne.
The improvements to Apple Maps aren’t solely visual additions – the app on the iPhone is also an invaluable guide for getting directions and finding places of interest.

For instance, those attending the F1 race can get directions to COTA and see where roads have been temporarily closed or redirected for the event. But it will also guide you to the section where you’re seated and help you find race-specific areas such as bathrooms and first aid areas.

Although the F1 race is a big reason for visiting Austin, it’s just one of many things to do in the state’s capitol. For that weekend and the rest of the year, Apple has created a new curated guide by country music singer-songwriter Dylan Gossett. You’ll find the race track (where Gossett once worked), as well as his favorite bar, the Armadillo Den, and his favorite guitar store, Moon Music Pro.
The Austin improvements to Apple Maps are available now on Apple devices and on the web.

articles.headline: 3 months after launch, Riot announces League of Legends Classic will be killed in January: 'most have gone back to other parts of League'
keyFacts: Riot announced that League of Legends Classic will go offline in January 2027 because most players returned to other parts of League.
A Riot spokesperson stated that the current season will be the last, with plans to potentially bring the mode back later as an event mode.
Riot confirmed that refunds will be issued for Classic content and at least seven more champions will still be rolled out.
body: League of Legends Classic was Riot's attempt to capitalise on nostalgia for vintage-era LoL. It stripped away most of the champions and kits introduced since 2013, reverted to an older version of the Summoner's Rift map, and promised to roll out "new" old Champions at a faster clip than in the olden days.
But the nostalgia Riot must have hoped would sustain the mode hasn't proven sufficient enough to keep it running: the mode will go offline in January 2027, only six months after its launch.
"We’ve seen a lot of players have fun revisiting the olden days with Classic," a Riot spokesperson wrote in a new update. "At this point though, most have gone back to other parts of League."
As a result, the current season will be the last. "We’ll then put Classic back in the box for now, with the goal of bringing it back, likely as an event mode with adjustments and additions."

It continues: "There’s more we’re going to share in the future about what we learned from this run. That includes where we think we got Classic right, where we could have gone more classic, and where sticking too closely to the past may have held the experience back."

Refunds will be issued for Classic content rendered obsolete by the closure. And it's not the end of the line yet: there are at least seven more Champions still to roll out, including Mordekaiser, Yorick, Hecarim and Lucian in the forthcoming 26.21 update, and Vilibear, Urgot and Udyr in future ones.

"This game mode was a true labor of love from so many Rioters, and seeing you all dive back in to reclaim the nostalgia, reconnect with old friends, and relive your glory days made it a truly special moment for everyone. We will keep exploring different ways to play League and as always, we appreciate all of your feedback. Every post on social media asking for Classic, every vote cast in the Council, and every minute spent leashing for your jungler again helped us bring this to life, so thank you very much."
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

What was wrong with Classic? Back in August, League of Legends esports veteran Alex Chu (also known as Xpecial) offered his thoughts on why uptake might be slow for players accustomed to modern LoL. His words came at a time when a lot of the LoL community were criticising the concept.

"Classic was never going to be a huge success at launch, because everyone has a different version of classic. I love this version. I recognize every champion and every item, and I know the ward system like the back of my hand. But most players started after me, and for them this isn't their classic, it's just an old game. The launch was always going to be a nostalgia bomb that fades. That part was priced in."
Chu then speculated a future for Classic that never eventuated, or at least, likely won't now.

"The interesting part is what happens now that the reins are loosened," he added. "We could end up with a version of League that players vote for things that would never fly with a mass audience. More complicated drafts. The ability to ban a champion for an entire season. Forcing a marksman mid meta or a mage bot meta just because the council wants to see it. Modern League can't do any of that, because modern League has to appeal to everyone. Classic only has to appeal to enough people."

Chu's thoughts aside, it's possible that old LoL just doesn't have the nostalgic appeal of old World of Warcraft, old Runescape, or old Guild Wars. Those are spaces you inhabit and they are generally less high pressure and adversarial. They become a kind of home away from home, whereas LoL is always just a hugely competitive MOBA. A good one that you can build a lifestyle around, but a MMORPG it ain't.

LoL also evolves much faster than those older MMOs did. Back in 2013, LoL was receiving new champions every two to three weeks, which could affect the whole experience. By contrast, MMOs at the time generally only received seismic updates on a yearly basis at most: much more time for a game condition to sink in.

With over ten years experience covering the games industry, his work has appeared on GamesRadar+, TechRadar, The Guardian, PLAY Magazine, the Sydney Morning Herald, and more. Specific interests include indie games, obscure Metroidvanias, speedrunning, experimental games and FPSs. He thinks Lulu by Metallica and Lou Reed is an all-time classic that will receive its due critical reappraisal one day.

articles.headline: Martinez releases statement to clarify outburst - but does not apologise
keyFacts: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez released a statement clarifying his criticism of the club's hierarchy after a Champions League defeat, but he did not apologize.
Martinez stated that his post-match outburst criticizing technical director Jason Wilcox and the club's transfer strategy stemmed from anger and frustration.
Club officials have not yet decided whether to discipline Martinez, while the boardroom and dressing room reacted with anger and bemusement.
body: Lisandro Martinez: Man Utd defender releases statement to clarify outburst but does not apologise

Man Utd defender Lisandro Martinez called out the club's hierarchy after their Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid; Martinez said he had expected more from "upstairs", singling out technical director Jason Wilcox
Wednesday 14 October 2026 23:53, UK
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has clarified his outburst after Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid in a statement - but stopped short of an apology.

Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club's hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat in Madrid, as he criticised the lack of summer investment in the squad, said he expected more from "upstairs" and singled out technical director Jason Wilcox.
But 24 hours on from his astonishing post-match interview, the Argentina international released a statement on Instagram on Wednesday night to clear up his comments.
- Lisandro Martinez outburst Q&A: Wilcox, transfer strategy and what next
- 'Awful' and 'disrespectful' - Carra and Rooney criticise Martinez outburst
- Martinez's Man Utd future in doubt after comments
He said: "Following everything that has been said about my comments yesterday, I want to share some thoughts on what I said and how I feel.
"After the match, I spoke out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted.

"Those who know me know how I live football, with passion, commitment and a huge desire to win. And when things don't go our way, it hurts, especially when representing a club with the history and stature of Manchester United.

"My words reflect how I feel and how much I want to see this club competing for the biggest honours. Those high standards are part of how I see football and the responsibility that comes with wearing this shirt.

"When I talk about wanting more, I'm talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.

"I know that, first and foremost, it's us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility. We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top.
"I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I'm convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment.
"My goal has been the same since day one, to win, to compete at the highest level and to give everything I have for this badge."
Sky Sports News' Football Correspondent Rob Dorsett:
There are real doubts about whether Martinez's contract will be extended when it expires in the summer.
United will focus on revamping their defence in the next transfer windows and have the formal option to prolong Martinez's stay for a further year.
Sky Sports News has also been told United are looking at new centre-backs, as well as left-backs.

United's bosses have yet to decide whether to discipline Martinez for his comments, when he said: "I expect more from our technical director [meaning director of football, Jason Wilcox]. We expect more from the top, from upstairs, to bring in more players to compete."

Sky Sports News has been told there is anger and bemusement at what Martinez said, both in the United boardroom and in the changing room, with at least one other player challenging him over his comments as the squad got on board the plane to fly back to Manchester.
It is also understood that there is no pressure on Wilcox internally regarding his position.
The implication that Martinez doesn't think his team-mates are good enough to compete has not gone down well with other players.
Martinez has been keen on a move away from Old Trafford for some time.

In the summer, he pushed for a move to Atletico Madrid, the side that beat United in the Champions League on Tuesday night, to follow his good friend and international team-mate, Cristian Romero, who left Spurs for Spain.
No suitable bid for Martinez came in for Manchester United to consider.
The 28-year-old made similar explosive comments about his bosses when at Ajax in 2022. Martinez, who again wanted a move away, called their sporting director Gerry Hamstra a "nobody".
Martinez remains a key part of Michael Carrick's squad and United's bosses know they have to handle this situation carefully.

articles.headline: Guardiola's return, Man City's defiance - and a game of glorious chaos
keyFacts: Pep Guardiola returned to watch Manchester City play following the club's guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial regulations.
Paris St-Germain scored three goals in a dominant first half before Manchester City staged a strong second-half revival, ultimately losing 4-2.
Manchester City returns to domestic competition to face Ipswich Town on Saturday while awaiting the outcome of their financial appeal.
body: - Published

Manchester City returned to the welcoming surroundings of home for the first time since being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations awash with defiance and presenting an 'us against the world' united front.

Pep Guardiola was back at the place he decorated with success for a decade in a public show of support to embattled chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano, the Catalan a low-key presence clad in a flat cap sitting a row behind the pair.
If his appearance was relatively under the radar, the fact that he chose a game certain to attract a global audience to make his return was heavy with significance.
Guardiola is ignoring the outside noise to back his former bosses to clear their name on appeal after the guilty verdict passed down by an independent commission.
The stand bearing his name was emblazoned with a 'CTID' - City 'Til I Die - mosaic, while the build-up to kick-off saw a display of fireworks and pyrotechnics worthy of several rock concerts.

The strategy to show an unabashed City ready to face down any enemy was going well, until the game kicked off and Champions League holders Paris St-Germain produced a ruthless first-half reality check cloaked within the brutal beauty of their football.
With City providing a dramatic backdrop off the pitch, the game more than matched the setting. A second-half revival ensured embarrassment was avoided - and instead gave us a classic.
City's first step back into the limelight on the hostile territory of Anfield on Sunday ended with a 3-0 win at Liverpool and wild celebrations.

Here, with Guardiola watching on from the directors' box with an agonised expression mirroring that of successor Enzo Maresca in his technical area, City ran headlong into a whirlwind of magnificent football from Luis Enrique's PSG, the half-time scoreline of 3-0 actually doing them a kindness.
To City's great credit, and also Maresca's after he made three half-time changes, they responded superbly after the break, creating a host of chances before eventually losing 4-2.
It did not retrieve what was lost in the first half, but it did at least allow City's fans to ramp up a frenzied atmosphere and give their team a rousing send-off at the final whistle.

In these surroundings, there was no question of any backlash against City's Abu Dhabi-based owners, despite the fact they were found guilty of such serious financial charges to leave the club in crisis and attracting pariah status.
The damage was done in PSG's staggering opening 45 minutes, with Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha the scorers as City were ripped apart.
A game that began in a wall of sound, with Guardiola's name resounding around the stadium at kick-off, was reduced to stunned silence in the first 15 minutes.
City, so composed and ordered amid the toxicity of Anfield on Sunday, were shell-shocked on home territory as even born streetfighters such as Enzo Fernandez were reduced to chasing shadows.

The players who rose in the face of the storm raging around Manchester City at Liverpool suddenly looked like they were carrying the weight of the world on their shoulders, which made their outstanding display after the break even more praiseworthy.
Guardiola looked just as engaged as when he was manager

Erling Haaland gave City hope, which looked to be snuffed out when goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, who had a very poor night against his former club, saved from Maghnes Akliouche, only to see the ball drop behind him into the net.
Guardiola sometimes looked just as engaged as he did when he prowled the touchline here at Etihad Stadium, collecting the trophies now being called into question.

When Josko Gvardiol had a header cleared off the line Guardiola clutched his face in anguish. When Haaland scored a goal that threatened to offer City an unlikely lifeline, he remained seated but pumped his fists into the air.
If the Catalan was a neutral observer, he would have relished a game of glorious chaos, the first half embellished by PSG before City mounted superb momentum after the break.
As a lover of pure football with the emphasis placed firmly on attack, he may have enjoyed it anyway. The post-match discussion with Maresca would certainly have had a busy agenda.
Maresca felt he saw enough to give City hope should they meet PSG again later in the Champions League, despite the manner in which they were dismantled in the first half.

"I really like playing against PSG because they are brave," said Maresca. "We know the way they want to press. They go man-to-man and they are very dynamic on the ball. They are the best team in Europe. They play fantastic football.

"But I think we are there. The reason why we struggled was because we conceded two early goals so quickly. When you are on the pitch you might think this is difficult, but in the second half we created enough to maybe deserve something.
"We feel sorry for the first half but I think we're quite happy now."
'Goals, goals and more goals'
Former Manchester City defender Nedum Onuoha, watching for Match of the Day, described it as "great entertainment", but "not a normal game of football".

"I don't feel like both teams were going at it at the same time," he said. "In the first half, PSG were excellent and City looked really off the pace. As a consequence they were heavily punished and the game basically left them.

"But then in the second half they have made some changes, they have rallied, knowing they are playing in front of their own crowd and their performance had to be better. So, it was more aggressive and more on the front foot, and that's why we saw those crazy scenes where it was shot after shot by City.

"If these two teams had played this game in matchweek six or seven, it would not have looked like this. There would have been more defensive solidity from both sides and they would probably have approached the game in a different manner.
"But at this stage, as we have kind of seen with some of the other games tonight, it is just goals, goals and more goals."

Either way, the superb Enrique remains the scourge of the Premier League, adding another win against City to a Champions League victims list that includes Liverpool, Aston Villa, Tottenham Hotspur and Arsenal, in a semi-final then last season's final.
Enrique is currently master of all he surveys in Europe as leader of this wonderful PSG team.

For Maresca and City, it is back to domestic business at home to Ipswich Town on Saturday â and all the uncertainty that brings with the Premier League in a state of limbo as they await sanctions and the result of their appeal.

articles.headline: McKinsey is making job applicants spar with a fake AI client
keyFacts: Consulting firm McKinsey & Company will require some entry-level job applicants to converse with a fake AI client during interviews, according to The Wall Street Journal.
The Wall Street Journal reported that the AI simulation aims to reflect 80% of daily consultant work scenarios, while human evaluators will assess the candidates.
The McKinsey tool is currently being tested for undergraduate business-analyst applicants in select offices.
body: Consulting firm McKinsey & Company is going to ask some entry-level candidates to have a 10-minute conversation with an AI simulation of a client as part of the interview process, according to The Wall Street Journal .

The AI simulation "aims to reflect 80% of the scenarios McKinsey consultants might encounter in their day-to-day work," the WSJ says, and it isn't designed to "mimic an unhinged client." The AI won't score the candidates - humans will be in the room to assess the candidates and see how well they deal with the simulated situations.

articles.headline: Trump is taking his midterms anger out on Ukraine
keyFacts: Ukraine says its access to SpaceX's Starlink and Starshield satellite systems is being throttled amid growing tensions with President Donald Trump.
Starlink and Starshield provide vital battlefield communications and control drones used in Ukraine's military efforts against Russia.
The United States has reportedly threatened to suspend intelligence sharing if Ukraine conducts more strikes on Russian oil refineries.
body: Donald Trump walks to the White House from the South Lawn on October 10, 2026. | Alex Wroblewski/AFP via Getty Images
This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here .
Welcome to The Logoff: Is Trump turning on Ukraine?

What’s happening? Ukraine says its access to Starlink, the satellite internet system run by Elon Musk’s SpaceX company, and Starshield, the military version of the same technology, is being throttled as President Donald Trump’s animosity toward the country mounts.

Why is Trump angry with Ukraine? Trump has been hot and cold on Ukraine since he returned to office, but his current anger is driven by oil prices and successful Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries — particularly ahead of the US midterm elections.

Last week, Trump announced a US-Russia diesel deal, which has elicited bipartisan anger and probably won’t do much , if anything, for diesel prices in the US. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has criticized the deal, leading Trump to lash out and call for Zelenskyy’s replacement.

Over the weekend, Trump also announced an “ENERGY CEASEFIRE” between Ukraine and Russia that doesn’t really seem to exist . “Both parties have agreed,” he wrote. “Do not break it!” (Russia appears to have broken it the same day , while Ukraine is complying for now.)

Is Ukraine actually to blame for high oil prices? Partially, but not primarily; as the BBC explains , while Ukrainian refinery strikes play a role, ongoing disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf oil industry from Trump’s war with Iran have had a greater impact (though Trump has tried to shift the blame to Ukraine).

Why is Starlink so important? Starlink and Starshield provide vital communications infrastructure in Ukraine, especially on the battlefield. The technology is also used to control offensive and defensive Ukrainian drones, which have emerged as a key part of Ukraine’s military efforts against Russia.

What’s next? Despite the fact that neither Russia nor Ukraine seemingly signed on to Trump’s “ENERGY CEASEFIRE” and Russia is still attacking Ukrainian energy facilities , Trump is trying to bind Ukraine to it: The US has reportedly threatened to suspend US intelligence sharing, which has helped give Ukraine early warning of Russian missile attacks, if Ukraine strikes more Russian refineries.
And with that, it’s time to log off…
